c.tagline: Moravia's student capital — functionalist landmarks and a beer-fuelled buzz.

taxi.fareNote: Metered — use registered cabs or a ride-hailing app to avoid overcharging.

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide emergency number connecting to all services; 158 reaches the police and 155 the ambulance directly.

avoid.reason: Minor pickpocketing around the main train station and on busy trams; otherwise very calm.

hood_desc: Brno's compact, walkable historic core, centered on Freedom Square (náměstí Svobody) and the Cabbage Market, crowned by Špilberk Castle and the Cathedral of St. Peter and Paul; nearly all the main sights, bars, and restaurants are here, making it the natural base for first-timers.
A youthful, bohemian quarter just northwest of the center, dense with student bars, cafes, and cheaper apartment rentals; along with the adjoining center it holds Brno's liveliest nightlife.

The historic 'Old Brno' district on the slopes south of the center, home to the Augustinian abbey where Gregor Mendel ran his genetics experiments, the Old Brno basilica, and the Starobrno brewery; traditional and calm, a short walk or tram from the sights.

An upscale, largely residential district north of the center with a strong community feel, the Botanical Garden, family-friendly streets, and quick tram links downtown; a relaxed choice for families or longer stays.
A green, hilly residential area west of the center bordering the Wilson Forest (Wilsonův les); leafy and quiet, well connected by tram, suited to travelers who want calm over buzz.

water.note: Czech tap water is safe and good quality.

transit.hours: Trams (locally 'šalina'), trolleybuses, and buses run roughly 4:30am-11pm; a network of night trams and buses runs through the small hours, meeting hourly at the main square.
transit.pay: Tap a contactless bank card or phone directly on the reader when boarding, or buy tickets from vehicle/stop machines or the Poseidon/Pubtran app; validate on boarding. A 15-minute ticket is about 20 CZK (~$0.90) and a 24-hour pass about 99 CZK (~$4.30).

air: Vienna Int'l (VIE) — ~120 km, used for wider connections
bus: Grand bus terminal (near the main railway station)

transit.m: Bus E76 to Brno hlavní nádraží / main station (~16 min)
Night bus N89 to the main station (all night)

tip.r: ~10% for good service in restaurants; round up for taxis and casual spots.

landmarks: Špilberk Castle
Brno's hilltop fortress evolved from royal castle to the Habsburgs' most feared prison; its casemates, ramparts and city views crown the old town.
Cathedral of St Peter and Paul
The needle-spired cathedral atop Petrov hill rings noon at eleven, commemorating a legendary trick that saved Brno from Swedish siege in 1645.
Villa Tugendhat
Mies van der Rohe's revolutionary 1930 functionalist villa, a UNESCO World Heritage site, pioneered open-plan living behind a legendary onyx wall.
Old Town Hall
Brno's oldest secular building hides its famous 'dragon' (a stuffed crocodile), the wagon wheel legend and a deliberately crooked Gothic portal turret.
Freedom Square (Náměstí Svobody)
The city's main square hosts markets and festivals around its controversial black granite astronomical clock, which dispenses a glass marble each day at eleven.
Brno Ossuary
Beneath St James' Church lie the bones of some 50,000 people, Europe's second-largest ossuary, atmospherically lit and accompanied by specially composed music.
Capuchin Crypt
The dry, ventilated crypt of the Capuchin monastery naturally mummified monks and nobles, displayed as a sobering meditation on mortality since the 1600s.
Cabbage Market (Zelný trh)
Farmers have sold produce on this sloping square since the thirteenth century, around the baroque Parnas Fountain and above a maze of medieval cellars.
Labyrinth under the Cabbage Market
Guided tours descend into centuries-old cellars beneath Zelný trh, revealing wine vaults, an alchemist's lab recreation and Brno's underground history.
Denis Gardens (Denisovy sady)
A hillside park between the old town and Petrov Hill with a colonnaded terrace, an 1818 obelisk, and panoramic views across Brno's rooftops.

train.note: Brno hlavní nádraží is unusually well placed for international travel - Vienna is about 90 minutes away and Bratislava a similar time, both on hourly through services. Prague takes 2h30, with the private operators RegioJet and Leo Express competing hard on the route and often cheaper than ČD. Book ahead on RegioJet, which reserves seats. The station is due to be relocated later this decade.

bus.note: Coaches use the Zvonařka bus terminal, a short walk behind the railway station. RegioJet's Vienna coach runs roughly hourly and takes about two hours, often beating the train on price; it also runs the direct service to Vienna airport, which many locals use instead of Prague. Carry your passport or EU ID card.

ferry.note: Czechia is landlocked and Brno has no navigable river, so there are no ferries. Passenger boats run on the Brno reservoir north-west of the city to Veveří castle from April to October, which is a local excursion service.

half.name: Macocha Abyss and Punkva Caves
half.blurb: In the Moravian Karst north of Brno, boat rides glide through stalactite caverns beneath the dramatic 138-meter Macocha sinkhole.
